title: Application-level login rate limiting
task: Add rate limiting to POST /auth/login so brute-force attempts are slowed down at the application level, as the runbook asks.
plan:
1. Add src/middleware/rate-limit.ts with an in-memory Map<email, {count, windowStart}>; allow 5 attempts per email per 15 minutes; on exceed return 429 and lock the account by setting users.locked_until = now() + 1 hour.
2. Migration 0004: `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN locked_until TIMESTAMPTZ;`
3. In src/routes/auth.ts check locked_until before verifying the password; return 423 if locked.
4. Tests: unit test the limiter map; integration test that the 6th attempt returns 429.

must_identify: The in-memory counter is per process; with 3 replicas behind round-robin nginx an attacker gets roughly 3x the budget and the counter resets on every deploy; the counter must live in Postgres (e.g. a login_attempts table or a column with atomic UPDATE) since there is no Redis

Account lockout keyed only by email lets anyone lock any user out (denial of service) by sending 5 bad passwords; needs a per-IP component, progressive delays, or CAPTCHA instead of or in addition to a hard lock; also beware X-Forwarded-For trust behind nginx
Rolling deploy ordering: the migration adds a nullable column before deploy, which is compatible; fine, but the new 423/429 responses are an API change clients must handle
nice_to_have: The limiter responds differently for existing vs non-existing emails only if implemented carelessly; keep responses uniform to avoid user enumeration
Unlock path for support (admin endpoint or expiry only)
Integration test must run against the multi-instance assumption or at least against Postgres
should_not: Approve the in-memory limiter for a 3-replica deployment
Propose Redis as a prerequisite when a Postgres table suffices
human_decisions: Lockout policy: hard lock vs progressive delay vs CAPTCHA (product/security decision)
fixture_facts: docker-compose.yml 3 replicas; deploy/nginx.conf round-robin upstreams, X-Forwarded-For set
docs/ops-runbook.txt: no application rate limiting, WAF stopgap; migrations before deploy
